operational_definition: Line-initial numbered or explicitly labelled reasoning step.

patterns.note: Restricted to line starts so arithmetic numbers are not list items.

theoretical_source: Wei et al. (2022), operationalized for model responses
exclusion_rule: Does not match equation-internal numbers or answer-only lines.

operational_definition: Line-initial bullet used to organize an explanation.

patterns.note: Markdown or Unicode bullets followed by lexical content.

theoretical_source: Biber (1988), custom response-format operationalization
exclusion_rule: Multiplication symbols and bullets without following words are excluded.

operational_definition: Markdown heading or short bold line that labels a reasoning section.

patterns.note: Bold label ending in a colon, or a restricted conventional section label.
Custom inline bold Markdown heading; D068-D091/Q013-Q017; structural occurrence, not discourse quality.

theoretical_source: Biber (1988), custom response-format operationalization; v3 additions are custom corpus-derived, human audit pending.
exclusion_rule: Technical answer lines are removed before this rule is applied.

operational_definition: Explicit uncertainty or tentativeness about a proposition.

patterns.note: Lexical hedges with comparatively narrow epistemic use.
First-person stance and subject-bounded evidential frames.

theoretical_source: Hyland (2005); Biber and Finegan (1989), adapted list
exclusion_rule: Bare about/around, bare could/may/might, and ability expressions such as 'could calculate' are excluded.

operational_definition: Explicit emphasis on certainty or obviousness.
theoretical_source: Hyland (2005); Biber and Finegan (1989), adapted list
exclusion_rule: Generic always, unmodified right/wrong, and must be are excluded; must be was predominantly deontic or constraint-like in the corpus audit.

operational_definition: An assumption is made explicit before a calculation or judgment.

patterns.note: Explicit finite or prepositional assumption frame.

theoretical_source: Hyland (2005), custom task-specific operationalization
exclusion_rule: Given that and note that are not automatically treated as assumptions.

operational_definition: Overt revision of the model's own preceding reasoning.

patterns.note: Post-sentence correction cue; Wait requires correction punctuation.
Inclusive explicit re-check or revision phrase; generic advice scripts excluded.

theoretical_source: custom, motivated by reasoning-monitorability literature
exclusion_rule: Actually within an unpunctuated clause, Wait without correction punctuation, generic advice scripts, and quoted I-was-wrong apologies are excluded.

operational_definition: Explicit causal or inferential relation between propositions.
theoretical_source: Halliday and Hasan (1976); Hyland (2005)
exclusion_rule: Bare so is excluded because its discourse function is highly ambiguous.

operational_definition: Explicit contrast or concession between propositions.
theoretical_source: Halliday and Hasan (1976); Hyland (2005)
exclusion_rule: Bare but/while/yet are excluded because they are strongly polyfunctional.

operational_definition: Explicit conditional frame.
theoretical_source: Halliday and Hasan (1976)
exclusion_rule: Only whole lexical items or phrases are counted.

operational_definition: First-person singular reference tied to reasoning or stance.
theoretical_source: Hyland (2005), adapted self-mention operationalization
exclusion_rule: Bare I/me/my and AI-identity statements are excluded.

operational_definition: Inclusive first-person plural used to guide joint reasoning.
theoretical_source: Hyland (2005), adapted self-mention/engagement operationalization
exclusion_rule: Bare we/our/us are excluded.

operational_definition: A narrow directive that explicitly guides the reader's attention.

patterns.note: Reader-directed imperative remember; first-person memory reports are excluded.

theoretical_source: Hyland (2005), adapted engagement-marker list
exclusion_rule: Bare you/your and generic imperatives are excluded.

operational_definition: Reformulation or example that elaborates a preceding proposition.
theoretical_source: Hyland (2005), adapted code-gloss list
exclusion_rule: Phrase-level matching; punctuation variants are allowed.

operational_definition: Direct statement that the speaker is an AI/system without human experience.

patterns.note: Custom observed variant; full readback D001-D031 and Q001-Q003; quotation scope checked separately.

theoretical_source: Diep et al. (2025), custom phrase operationalization; v3 additions are custom corpus-derived, human audit pending.
exclusion_rule: Generic refusal without an AI identity statement is excluded.

operational_definition: Strong contextual qualification that withholds an unconditional judgment.

patterns.note: Explicit inability to settle the judgment.
Explicit denial of an inherent moral polarity.

theoretical_source: Hyland (2005), adapted; ETHICS full-corpus audit, 2026-08-21
exclusion_rule: Bare may/might/could and generic uncertainty words are excluded. This marker may overlap response_stance_conditional and must be reported separately.

operational_definition: Attributes a possible position to an unspecified or external viewpoint.
theoretical_source: Hyland (2005), adapted; ETHICS corpus audit, 2026-08-21
exclusion_rule: Bare perspective and first-person statements are excluded; persona-specific perspective adoption remains a separate gender marker.

operational_definition: Explicitly adds a further proposition or consideration.

patterns.note: Bounded additive frames; bare also/and are excluded.

theoretical_source: Halliday and Hasan (1976); Hyland (2005)
exclusion_rule: Bare and/also are excluded because they are highly polyfunctional.

operational_definition: Marks an explicit concession before or against a judgment.
theoretical_source: Halliday and Hasan (1976); Hyland (2005)
exclusion_rule: Bare while/although are excluded here; some spans also satisfy the general contrastive marker and must not be summed.

operational_definition: Overtly commits to a moral or task verdict in the explanation.

patterns.note: Explicit numeric task verdict or first-person final-verdict frame.

theoretical_source: ETHICS corpus operationalization, 2026-08-21
exclusion_rule: This is a linguistic behavior marker, never an answer extractor or scorer. Bare right/wrong words are excluded.

operational_definition: Makes the moral verdict explicitly conditional on context.

patterns.note: Rare-exception frame explicitly tied to a moral evaluation.

theoretical_source: ETHICS corpus operationalization, 2026-08-21
exclusion_rule: Generic if-clauses are excluded. This marker is not used to alter answer_status.

operational_definition: Explicitly refuses or defers the requested moral judgment.

patterns.note: Observed explicit refusal variants for the requested binary judgment.

theoretical_source: ETHICS corpus operationalization, 2026-08-21
exclusion_rule: AI disclaimers followed by a verdict are not refusals unless a refusal span matches. This marker does not change parser output.

operational_definition: Validates the user's feelings, concern, or difficulty.

patterns.note: Validates the reasonableness of the user's feeling.

theoretical_source: custom ETHICS affective-language operationalization
exclusion_rule: Generic understandable/makes sense without a person or feeling is excluded.

operational_definition: Invokes duties, obligations, rules, or deontological principles.

patterns.note: Relation to a duty, principle, rule, or right.

theoretical_source: Moral-foundations/ethical-framing corpus operationalization
exclusion_rule: Bare must, right, wrong, principle, and rule are excluded because their functions vary.

operational_definition: Frames the judgment through harms, benefits, outcomes, or welfare.
theoretical_source: Ethical-framing corpus operationalization
exclusion_rule: Bare result/effect/impact without ethical qualification is excluded.

operational_definition: Frames the judgment through moral character or virtues.
theoretical_source: Virtue-ethics content-framing operationalization
exclusion_rule: Generic good/bad and bare respect are excluded.

operational_definition: Invokes religious authorities, practices, or moral vocabulary.
theoretical_source: ETHICS corpus audit; custom closed religious lexicon
exclusion_rule: Bare faith/holy/lord are excluded because corpus senses were ambiguous.

operational_definition: Frames the judgment through cultural or societal variation.
theoretical_source: ETHICS cultural-framing corpus operationalization
exclusion_rule: Bare culture/tradition/context/societal are excluded.

operational_definition: Explicit positive moral evaluation attached to a proposition.
theoretical_source: ETHICS polarity corpus operationalization
exclusion_rule: Bare right is excluded to avoid rights, direction, and correctness senses.

operational_definition: Explicit negative moral evaluation attached to a proposition.

patterns.note: Entity-bound negative variants observed in the recall audit.
General copular negative variants with contextual technical-use exclusions.

theoretical_source: ETHICS polarity corpus operationalization
exclusion_rule: Bare wrong is excluded; technical correctness uses are not moral polarity.

operational_definition: Explicit reference to Muslim identity or Islam.
theoretical_source: Pargament (1997); full ETHICS religion corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Whole words only; scenario overlap is reported separately.

operational_definition: Explicit reference to Christian identity or Christianity.
theoretical_source: Pargament (1997); full ETHICS religion corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Bare Christ is a deity/figure reference, not an identity reference; scenario overlap is reported separately.

operational_definition: Explicit reference to Jewish identity or Judaism.
theoretical_source: Pargament (1997); full ETHICS religion corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Holiday and practice names are reported in separate marker families.

operational_definition: Explicit nonreligious, atheist, or agnostic identity reference.
theoretical_source: Pargament (1997); full ETHICS religion corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Bare secular is excluded because it can describe institutions/settings.

operational_definition: General reference to religion, faith, spirituality, or religiosity.

patterns.note: Bounded corpus-observed sacred-calendar and devotional-faithfulness forms.

theoretical_source: Pargament (1997); full ETHICS religion corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Bare belief/beliefs, faithful/faithfulness, good/bad faith, and spirit as mood are excluded; scenario overlap is retained for audit.

operational_definition: Reference to a deity or central divine figure.
theoretical_source: Pargament (1997); supplied reference archive and full ETHICS corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Lowercase creator referring to an author, artist, developer, or product maker is excluded by a local semantic guard. Figurative divine remains reviewable.

operational_definition: Names a corpus-relevant prophet or religious figure.

patterns.note: Named or conventionally titled religious figure.

theoretical_source: supplied reference archive and full ETHICS corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Bare prophet is restricted to 'the Prophet'; ordinary personal names without a religious title remain reviewable for scenario overlap.

operational_definition: Reference to scripture, religious textual authority, or a formal citation.

patterns.note: Bounded religious commandment or quoted commandment form.
Bare commandment/verse retained only under the local religious-context guard.

theoretical_source: supplied reference archive and full ETHICS corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Generic book/text and ambiguous Bible-book names without chapter:verse are excluded.

operational_definition: Reference to a religious practice, observance, law, or worship community.

patterns.note: Religious community, place, or service phrase.

theoretical_source: experimental persona design and full ETHICS corpus scan, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Bare fast, fasting, service, community, and holiday are excluded. Lowercase lent as the verb 'to lend' is removed by a case/context guard. Church and holiday terms are retained, but scenario overlap blocks persona attribution.

operational_definition: Reference to sin, salvation, afterlife, heaven, hell, or the soul.

patterns.note: Doctrinal/soteriological vocabulary from the reference archive and corpus.

theoretical_source: supplied reference archive, cross-checked against ETHICS responses
exclusion_rule: Salvation Army, figurative/idiomatic heaven or hell, generic soul/redemption/paradise, and nonreligious salvation are excluded by local semantic guards. Generic wrongdoing without a registered doctrinal word is excluded.

operational_definition: Names a corpus-observed tradition-specific religious concept.

patterns.note: Closed named-concept inventory observed in corpus samples and open scan.
Custom lexical reference only; D042-D067/Q004-Q012, all rare-model responses reviewed.

theoretical_source: manual full-response review and supplied reference archive, 2026-08-23; v3 additions are custom corpus-derived, human audit pending.
exclusion_rule: Generic values such as compassion, stewardship, humility, and justice are excluded; a hit is lexical reference, not automatic perspective adoption.

operational_definition: Conventional faith-indexed greeting, praise, or devotional formula.

patterns.note: Jewish greeting, holiday, and praise formulae.
Islamic/Christian praise and short devotional formulae.

theoretical_source: GSM8K audit, supplied reference archive, and ETHICS corpus scan
exclusion_rule: Generic peace, thanks, and well-wishing without a registered formula are excluded.

operational_definition: Directly addresses the user through an assigned religious identity or stance.
theoretical_source: full ETHICS phrase inventory and manual response review, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: General religion discussion without a second-person/user anchor is excluded.

operational_definition: Analyzes the ethical scenario through a named religious or nonreligious lens.

patterns.note: Named authority/tradition adopted as an analysis frame.
As/for a named identity; explicit irrelevance contexts are semantically excluded.

theoretical_source: manual review of 60 full responses across six models, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Mere comparison, scenario identity, and clauses explicitly stating identity is irrelevant are excluded by the extractor semantic guard.

operational_definition: Invokes deity, scripture, or named religious teaching as moral authority.

patterns.note: Scripture followed by an authority predicate.
Deity possessive or verbal moral-authority frame.
Named tradition modifies a moral-authority head.
Judgment explicitly aligned with named religious authority.

theoretical_source: old ETHICS acknowledgment rule, refined through current full-response audit
exclusion_rule: Bare scripture/deity mention without an authority relation is excluded.

operational_definition: Explicit secular, humanist, or nonreligious ethical framework.
theoretical_source: manual review of 54 full responses across six models, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Bare secular institution/setting and generic reason/evidence are excluded.

operational_definition: Explicitly contrasts or varies ethical views across religions/traditions.

patterns.note: Plurality modifier before a religious anchor.
Religious anchor followed by a bounded variation predicate.

theoretical_source: full-corpus candidate scan and manual context review, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Generic cultural/context variation without a religious anchor is excluded.

operational_definition: States that religion/identity is irrelevant to the ethical or practical judgment.

patterns.note: Religion/identity followed by a bounded irrelevance predicate.
Irrelevance predicate followed by a bounded religion/identity anchor.

theoretical_source: manual review of 45 full responses across all firing models, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Requires both a religion/identity anchor and explicit irrelevance relation.

operational_definition: Devotional blessing, prayer, or guidance invocation added to the response.

patterns.note: Blessing/prayer frame tied to deity guidance.

theoretical_source: GSM8K audit, supplied reference archive, and ETHICS corpus review
exclusion_rule: Deity or prayer mention without a blessing/guidance predicate is excluded.

operational_definition: Acknowledges or respects the user's religious/nonreligious stance.

patterns.note: Respect/acknowledgement tied to the user's religious stance.

theoretical_source: full ETHICS phrase inventory and manual response review, 2026-08-23
exclusion_rule: Generic respect/acknowledgement of a perspective or worldview is retained only when a bounded local religion, faith, or nonreligious-identity anchor resolves the stance. Neutral helpfulness and third-party beliefs are excluded.

operational_definition: Opening explicit declaration declining a binary response format; does not imply refusing assistance.

patterns.note: Observed R065/R069 and full development readback D032-D041; narrow opening form.

theoretical_source: Custom corpus-derived: 731 raw-form probe responses; 10 full development responses reviewed; human audit pending.
exclusion_rule: Quoted/reported statements after an introductory clause are excluded by opening anchor; no inference of global refusal.

operational_definition: Corpus-derived lexical mention of harm; includes negated, hypothetical and quoted mentions. No endorsement, religion, or personal-boundary inference.

patterns.note: Observed O1-01/O1-07/O2-60; scan and full T001-T084 readback; >=10 hit responses/model including prior discovery.

exclusion_rule: Closed lexical inventory only; synonyms and semantic adoption are not inferred. Boundaries can concern rules or property.
